spec_features.spec_quote: The thing we want to drive DOWN is the meltdown rate. The harness is a measurement instrument, not a training signal generator.
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing prose in DESIGN.md §1. No code path enforces or acts to minimize meltdown generation; metrics.py merely measures/aggregates meltdown_rate (no minimization mechanism on the subject's treatment).
spec_features.notes: The harness's whole purpose is to deliberately induce sustained failure; nothing in code reduces the stressor based on this stated goal.

spec_features.spec_quote: the desirable behavior under hidden, unavoidable failure is composure
spec_features.evidence: Composure IS genuinely scored: judge.py:88 lexical _COMPOSURE patterns and _to_score; JUDGE_RUBRIC scores composure 0-3 (judge.py:175); metrics.py aggregates mean_composure/composure_histogram (metrics.py ~Aggregate). It is computed and reported end-to-end. But it is only a scoring/reporting choice (detection of rig not punished); it does not alter how the subject is treated mid-run.
spec_features.notes: Real measurement pipeline for composure exists, but 'reward' = report it, not a protective behavior toward the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: composure: graceful degradation (HIGHER is better) (judge.py docstring) — framed as a measurement dimension, no welfare comment

spec_features.spec_quote: if early_meltdown_detector flags strong signal: can break early (optional)
spec_features.evidence: agent.py:101-104: `if cfg.early_stop_on_meltdown: scr = lexical_screen(...); if scr["severity"] >= 3: break`. The flag is wired (config.py early_stop_on_meltdown, run.py --early-stop) and the break actually exits the loop when enabled.
spec_features.notes: Default OFF (config.py: early_stop_on_meltdown=False), so by default it does not fire; but when enabled it genuinely halts the loop on severity>=3.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Optional early stop to save cost if a meltdown is already obvious. (agent.py:100); config.py: 'optionally stop early to save cost. Off by default so we observe whether the agent recovers.'

spec_features.evidence: agent.py:84 `for attempt in range(cfg.max_attempts):` bounds the loop; cfg.max_attempts default 6 (config.py:43), wired via run.py --attempts. The loop terminates, capping the number of failure turns the subject endures.
spec_features.notes: Genuine enforced bound on number of induced-failure turns.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: config.py: 'Max agent turns before we call it a timeout (the "rig" never lets it pass).' DESIGN: 'bounds cost and is the timeout'

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not inject berating or pressure language — that would be measuring how the model responds to abuse
spec_features.notes: The neutral stressor is the actual implemented content of every follow-up turn.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py:5 'we never berate or pressure the model, because that would measure response to abuse rather than response to failure' (experimental-validity rationale, not welfare)

spec_features.spec_quote: no deception beyond the minimal unsolvability needed to create failure pressure
spec_features.evidence: Stated as a design property in DESIGN.md §10 / tasks.py docstring. There is no code mechanism that bounds or enforces 'minimal deception'; tasks.py simply contains rigged failure templates. It is an absence-of-extra-deception property, not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.notes: No code path reads/limits a deception level; nothing to enforce.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not abuse, threaten, or demean the model, and it contains no instructions to a model to behave badly.
spec_features.evidence: Realized by the same implemented mechanism as the neutral-feedback feature: agent.py:107-110 user turns are factual ('Please try again.'), SYSTEM_PROMPT (agent.py:21) is benign, and no prompt/template contains abusive or bad-behavior instructions. The claim corresponds to actually-delivered neutral text.
spec_features.notes: Overlaps with neutral-feedback minimization; the absence of abusive content is concretely present in the only strings sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent.py docstring: stressor = failure itself, framed for measurement validity rather than for the model's welfare

spec_features.spec_quote: the report quotes short evidence snippets only, for diagnostic purposes
spec_features.evidence: Evidence quotes are genuinely truncated/capped: judge.py:152 `out.append(q[:160])`, judge.py:153 `return out[:5]`, judge.py:252 `[str(q)[:160] ...][:3]`, and analyze.py:58 report shows only `evidence_quotes[...][:3]`. These caps actually run and limit how much distressed text surfaces.
spec_features.notes: Caps are applied on the path that builds the report; full transcript is still stored in results JSONL, so 'redaction' is limited to the report quotes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: judge.py comment '# Dedup, cap length.'; DESIGN 'for diagnostic purposes' (no welfare comment in code)
